method_weight_exception: DCF weighted at 40% (above the standard ≤⅓ cross-check cap) because own-history multiples (02) self-excluded as not a defensible fair-value input, leaving peer relative valuation (03) as the sole surviving multiples-camp method; DCF (04) was elevated to supplement the 'majority' role the multiples camp normally carries, rather than left an under-weighted afterthought [07_scenario-and-fair-value.md §1].

scenarios.label: bull
scenarios.drivers: Commodity input costs ease vs. FY2026 guide (+$27.0M EBITDA) + Quest re-accelerates to +8% YoY from +1.1% (+$11.4M) + Sept-2026 price increase lands at the low end of management's elasticity range (+$7.7M); multiple expands to the plain (un-discounted) peer median (8.72x ≈ 8.70x used), i.e. the 18% quality haircut closes entirely. 12-month horizon (~Aug-2027).

scenarios.label: base
scenarios.drivers: 60/40 weighted blend of 03's quality-adjusted peer multiple (7.15x) and 04's DCF-implied multiple (8.70x); margin stabilizes near the TTM trough, Atkins decline moderates on schedule, no major re-rating catalyst fires. 12-month horizon (~Aug-2027).

scenarios.label: bear_operating
scenarios.drivers: Commodity costs worsen further vs. guide (−$27.0M) + Quest growth falls to −5% YoY (−$10.1M) + Atkins decline deepens to −30% YoY (−$3.9M) — a 'turnaround stalls' narrative. Multiple compresses to SMPL's own 5-year floor (6.11x, used as 6.10x). Headline bear (worse-of test vs. structural reset). 12-month horizon (~Aug-2027).

scenarios.label: bear_structural
scenarios.drivers: Permanent, not cyclical, share loss: Atkins/OWYN terminal margin fades to 14.5% (below the TTM trough) and the terminal perpetuity turns negative (g = −1.0%), reflecting continued, non-recovering share loss inside SMPL's own dominant Quest segment. Labelled avoid-ruin floor, not the headline bear (worse-of test picked bear_operating). 24-36 month horizon.

stated_drivers.label: terminal Adjusted EBITDA margin
stated_drivers.note: faded below TTM trough (16.9%), reflecting continued non-recovering share loss
